Evaluator throws propagate with nothing committed —\n        // a throwing evaluator must never terminally skip.\n        const snapshot = await opts.readCurrentSnapshot();\n        const verdict = opts.evaluateGuard(predicate, opts.frozenInputs, snapshot);\n        if (verdict !== true) {\n            const pinned = await pinFanoutChildTerminal({\n                store: opts.store,\n                childRow: current,\n                result: { kind: \"skipped\", reason: \"non-applicable\" },\n                nowMs: opts.meta.nowMs,\n                policy: opts.policy,\n                meta: opts.meta,\n                producers,\n                what: \"guard-false skip\",\n            });\n            return { status: \"skipped\", outcome: pinned.outcome, row: pinned.row };\n        }\n    }\n    if (fence !== undefined && (await fence.revalidateAuthority()) !== true) {\n        const pinned = await pinFanoutChildTerminal({\n            store: opts.store,\n            childRow: current,\n            result: {\n                kind: \"failed\",\n                reason: producers.outcome.FANOUT_T32_REFUSAL_REASON,\n            },\n            nowMs: opts.meta.nowMs,\n            policy: opts.policy,\n            meta: opts.meta,\n            producers,\n            what: \"refused-revoked\",\n        });\n        return { status: \"refused-revoked\", outcome: pinned.outcome, row: pinned.row };\n    }\n    const running = producers.tables.withFanoutRowData(current, { ...data, state: \"running\" }, opts.meta);\n    try {\n        await opts.store.commit({\n            expectedRevision: await opts.store.readRevision(),\n            writes: [\n                {\n                    kind: \"update\",\n                    model: T34F7_FANOUT_CHILD_MODEL,\n                    id: current.id,\n                    expectedVersion: current.version,\n                    row: running,\n                },\n            ],\n            history: [],\n            receipt: null,\n            outbox: [],\n            schedules: [],\n            uniqueClaims: [],\n            uniqueReleases: [],\n        });\n    }\n    catch (error) {\n        if (fanoutStateErrorCode(error) !== null)\n            throw error;\n        if (!isFanoutFenceConflict(error, producers) && !isFanoutStorageConstraint(error, producers)) {\n            throw error;\n        }\n        // Lost race: observe the winner. Terminal replays, running\n        // holds, still-pending reads stale (the world moved; re-drive).\n        const reloaded = await opts.store.load(T34F7_FANOUT_CHILD_MODEL, key);\n        if (reloaded === null) {\n            throw new Error(\"t34-f7: claim: child row vanished under a claim race.\");\n        }\n        const reloadedData = producers.tables.readFanoutChildRow(reloaded);\n        const replayed = fanoutChildOutcomeFromData(reloadedData);\n        if (replayed !== null) {\n            return { status: \"replayed\", outcome: replayed, row: reloaded };\n        }\n        if (reloadedData.state === \"running\") {\n            return { status: \"held\", row: reloaded, child: opts.child };\n        }\n        return { status: \"refused-stale\", row: reloaded, child: opts.child };\n    }\n    return { status: \"claimed\", row: running, child: opts.child };\n}\n/**\n * T34-F7: record one executed attempt durably — terminal replays,\n * live-but-idle throws (record needs a running claim), then\n * completed/skipped/failed record terminally (outcome + checkpoint\n * advance in ONE linkage-asserted batch) while transient retries\n * within budget or exhausts to failed/exhausted (F3-exact: attempt\n * cap OR time horizon; attempts++ on the same row identity).\n *\n * The retry horizon anchors at `fanoutFirstAttemptAnchor` (the child\n * row's durable `created` — the F3/F5-owed seam): crash-stable,\n * enforced from durable truth. (await loadFanoutStateProducers());\n    checkFanoutRowMeta(opts.meta, \"record\");\n    checkFanoutPolicy(opts.policy, \"record\");\n    checkFanoutAttemptResult(opts.result);\n    if (!Number.isFinite(opts.nowMs) || opts.nowMs < 0) {\n        throw new Error(\"t34-f7: record needs nowMs as finite epoch ms >= 0.\");\n    }\n    producers.cohort.checkFanoutChildId(opts.child);\n    const key = producers.tables.fanoutChildRowId(opts.child.parentOccurrence, opts.child.handler, opts.child.recordId);\n    const current = await opts.store.load(T34F7_FANOUT_CHILD_MODEL, key);\n    if (current === null) {\n        throw new Error(`t34-f7: no fanout child row for ${JSON.stringify(key)} (producer write missing).`);\n    }\n    const data = producers.tables.readFanoutChildRow(current);\n    const terminal = fanoutChildOutcomeFromData(data);\n    if (terminal !== null) {\n        return { status: \"replayed\", outcome: terminal, row: current };\n    }\n    if (data.state !== \"running\") {\n        throw new Error(`t34-f7: record applies to running children only; ${JSON.stringify(key)} is ${data.state}.`);\n    }\n    const staged    producers.join.assertFanoutChildJoin(batch);\n    try {\n        await opts.store.commit(batch);\n    }\n    catch (error) {\n        if (fanoutStateErrorCode(error) !== null)\n            throw    };\n}\n/**\n * T34-F7: release running children whose claim is provably stale\n * (F4 `resume` posture: `updated` + max age <= now, boundary\n * inclusive) back to pending for re-drive.  cursor: opts.cursor,\n        limit: opts.limit,\n    });\n    const page = producers.tables.fanoutChildPageResult(await opts.store.query(query), opts.limit);\n    const released = [];\n    const         kind: \"update\",\n                        model: T34F7_FANOUT_CHILD_MODEL,\n                        id: row.id,\n                        expectedVersion: row.version,\n uniqueClaims: [],\n                uniqueReleases: [],\n            });\n        }\n        catch (error) {\n            if (fanoutStateErrorCode(error) !== null)\n                throw error;\n            if (!isFanoutFenceConflict(error, producers) && !isFanoutStorageConstraint(error, producers)) {\n                throw error;\n            }\n            skipped.push({ childId: data.childId,            ? \"completed\"\n            : terminal.cause.kind === \"skipped\" || terminal.cause.kind === \"failed\"\n                ? `${terminal.state}/${terminal.cause.reason}`\n                : cohort.anchor }),\n    });\n    if (lifecycle.status === \"deleted\") {\n        return tryPin(childRow, { kind: \"skipped\", reason: \"deleted\" }, \"turn pin deleted\");\n    }\n    if     ...(cohort.anchor === undefined ? {} : { anchor: cohort.anchor }),\n        });\n        if (raced.status === \"deleted\") {\n            return tryPin(childRow, { kind: \"skipped\", reason: `Invalid input on operation ${JSON.stringify(opName)}: inputs need non-empty names.`);\n    }\n    const name = value['name'];\n    const what = `input ${JSON.stringify(name)} on operation ${JSON.stringify(kind)} for ${what}; ` +\n            'supported: ref, string, integer, decimal, money, datetime, boolean, file, enum.');\n    }\n    if (typeof value['required'] !== 'boolean') {\n        fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: required must be a boolean.`);\n    }\n    const required = value['required'];\n    const fallback = checkDefault(value['default'], what);\n    if (kind === 'ref') {\n        if (typeof value['model'] !== 'string' || value['model'] === '') {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: ref inputs name a non-empty model.`);\n        }\n        if (typeof value['versioned'] !== 'boolean') {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: versioned must be a boolean.`);\n        }\n        const model = value['model'];\n        if (!modelNames.has(model)) {\n            fail('dangling_reference', `Invalid ${what}: model ${JSON.stringify(model)} has no descriptor in this set.`);\n        }\n        return {\n            name,\n            kind: 'ref',\n            model: model,\n            versioned: value['versioned'],\n            required,\n            ...(fallback !== undefined ? { default: fallback } : {}),\n        };\n    }\n    if (kind === 'enum') {\n        const values = value['enumValues'];\n        if (!Array.isArray(values) ||\n            values.some((entry) => typeof entry !== 'string' || entry === '')) {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: enum inputs carry enumValues as an array of non-empty strings.`);\n        }\n        return {\n            name,\n            kind: 'enum',\n            required,\n            enumValues: [...values],\n            ...(fallback !== undefined ? { default: fallback } : {}),\n        };\n    }\n    if (value['enumValues'] !== undefined) {\n        fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: enumValues is present exactly for enum.`);\n    }\n    return {\n        name,\n        kind: kind,\n        required,\n        ...(fallback !== undefined ? { default: fallback } : {}),\n    };\n}\n/** Validate one canonical model descriptor; returns the model name. */\nfunction checkCanonicalModel(value) {\n    if (!isRecord(value) || typeof value['name'] !== 'string' || value['name'] === '') {\n        fail('malformed_descriptor', 'Invalid model descriptor: models need non-empty names.');\n    }\n    const name = value['name'];\n    if (!isRecord(value['fields'])) {\n        fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid model ${JSON.stringify(name)}: fields must be an object.`);\n    }\n    const fields = {};\n    for (const [fieldName, fieldValue] of Object.entries(value['fields'])) {\n        const what = `field ${JSON.stringify(fieldName)} on model ${JSON.stringify(name)}`;\n        if (fieldName === '' || fieldName.includes('.')) {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: field names are non-empty single segments.`);\n        }\n        if (!isRecord(fieldValue)) {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: field defs must be objects.`);\n        }\n        if (typeof fieldValue['required'] !== 'boolean' || typeof fieldValue['serverOnly'] !== 'boolean') {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: required and serverOnly must be booleans.`);\n        }\n        let array;\n        if (fieldValue['array'] !== undefined) {\n            const marker = fieldValue['array'];\n            if (!isRecord(marker) || typeof marker['required'] !== 'boolean') {\n                fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: array markers carry a boolean required.`);\n            }\n            array = { required: marker['required'] };\n        }\n        const fallback = checkDefault(fieldValue['default'], what);\n        fields[fieldName] = {\n            required: fieldValue['required'],\n            serverOnly: fieldValue['serverOnly'],\n            ...(array !== undefined ? { array } : {}),\n            ...(fallback !== undefined ? { default: fallback } : {}),\n        };\n    }\n    if (typeof value['deleteMode'] !== 'string' || !KNOWN_DELETE_MODES.has(value['deleteMode'])) {\n        fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid model ${JSON.stringify(name)}: deleteMode is archive, remove, or none.`);\n    }\n    let uniqueKeys;\n    if (value['uniqueKeys'] !== undefined) {\n        if (!Array.isArray(value['uniqueKeys'])) {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid model ${JSON.stringify(name)}: uniqueKeys must be an array.`);\n        }\n        for (const key of value['uniqueKeys']) {\n            if (typeof key !== 'string' || key === '') {\n                fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid model ${JSON.stringify(name)}: unique keys are non-empty field names.`);\n            }\n            if (key.includes(',')) {\n                fail('unsupported_composite_unique', `Model ${JSON.stringify(name)} declares composite unique ${JSON.stringify(key)}; ` +\n                    'composite uniques need T04b and cannot load in the T16a core scope.');\n            }\n            if (!Object.hasOwn(fields, key)) {\n                fail('dangling_reference', `Unknown unique-key field ${JSON.stringify(key)} on model ${JSON.stringify(name)}.`);\n            }\n        }\n        uniqueKeys = [...value['uniqueKeys']];\n    }\n    return {\n        name: name,\n        fields,\n        deleteMode: value['deleteMode'],\n        ...(uniqueKeys !== undefined ? { uniqueKeys } : {}),\n    };\n}\n/**\n * Core-scope executability: CRUD descriptors must carry what the generated\n * executor consumes. Creates resolve their model from the `<Model>.create`\n * emission convention; updates/deletes carry the synthesized versioned\n * `record` ref (identity + fencing — an unversioned or missing target\n * cannot execute; extra ref FIELD inputs beside it are ordinary values).\n * Reads/scenarios need no structural shape here (reads admit for\n * denied-not-unknown; scenarios run through the caller's execute seam).\n */\nfunction checkCrudExecutable(descriptor, modelNames) {\n    const name = descriptor.name;\n    if (descriptor.kind === 'create') {\n        if (!name.endsWith('.create') || name.length === '.create'.length) {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid create operation ${JSON.stringify(name)}: core-scope creates are ` +\n                'named <Model>.create.');\n        }\n        const model = name.slice(0, -'.create'.length);\n        if (!modelNames.has(model)) {\n            fail('dangling_reference', `Invalid create operation ${JSON.stringify(name)}: model ${JSON.stringify(model)} ` +\n                'has no descriptor in this set.');\n        }\n        return;\n    }\n    if (descriptor.kind === 'update' || descriptor.kind === 'delete') {\n        const record = descriptor.inputs.find((input) => input.kind === 'ref' && input.name === 'record');\n        if (record?.versioned !== true) {\n            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${descriptor.kind} operation ${JSON.stringify(name)}: core-scope ` +\n                `${descriptor.kind}s carry a versioned \"record\" ref.`);\n        }\n    }\n}\n/**\n * Load a validated `ExecutionDescriptorSet` into an admission-ready registry.\n * `contractVersion` must equal 1; unknown operation/input kinds reject the\n * WHOLE set — nothing is registered on any failure. Engine-local `by`/`when`\n * policy maps onto every generated operation (see `LoadDescriptorSetOptions`).\n */\nexport function loadExecutionDescriptorSet(set, opts) {\n    if (!isRecord(set)) {\n        fail('malformed_descriptor', 'Invalid descriptor set: the set must be an object.');\n    }\n    // Exact version match first: a version mismatch is the precise error, never\n    // a silent fallback onto older/newer intake rules.\n    if (set['contractVersion'] !== EXECUTION_CONTRACT_VERSION) {\n        fail('version_mismatch', `Incompatible descriptor set: contractVersion guards mixed-version assembly\n    // (values/identity/wire/examples pins are checked by L7 activation, which\n    // owns `requires` fulfillment).\n    if (STATE_CONTRACT_VERSION !== T04A_PINNED_VERSIONS.state) {\n        fail('version_mismatch', `Incompatible state contract: loaded ${STATE_CONTRACT_VERSION}, ` +\n            `required ${T04A_PINNED_VERSIONS.state}.`);\n    }\n    if (!Array.isArray(set['operations']) || !Array.isArray(set['models'])) {\n        fail('malformed_descriptor', 'Invalid descriptor set: operations and models must be arrays.');\n    }\n    const models = [];\n    const modelNames = new Set();\n    for (const model of set['models']) {\n        const checked = checkCanonicalModel(model);\n        const name = checked.name;\n        if (modelNames.has(name)) {\n            fail('duplicate_name', `Duplicate model descriptor: ${JSON.stringify(name)}.`);\n        }\n        modelNames.add(name);\n        models.push(checked);\n    }\n operation['kind'];\n        if (typeof kind !== 'string' || !KNOWN_OPERATION_KINDS.has(kind)) {\n            fail('unknown_operation_kind', `Unknown operation kind ${JSON.stringify(kind)} on fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid operation ${JSON.stringify(opName)}: inputs must be an array.`);\n        }\n        const inputs = [];\n        const seenInputs = new Set();\n        for (const input of operation['inputs']) {\n            const checked = checkCanonicalInput(input, opName, modelNames);\n            if (seenInputs.has(checked.name)) {\n                fail('duplicate_name',     const descriptor = {\n            name: opName,\n            kind: kind,\n            inputs,\n        };\n        checkCrudExecutable(descriptor, modelNames);\n        // Engine-local policy validateByPredicate(by, `generated by for operation ${JSON.stringify(opName)}`);\n        let when;\n        if (opts.when !== undefined) {\n            const raw = typeof opts.when === 'function' ?                   throw new Error(`Invalid generated when for operation ${JSON.stringify(opName)}: ` +\n                        `${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`);\n                }\n                try {\n                    when = structuredClone(raw);\n                }\n                catch {\n                    throw new Error(`Invalid generated when for operation frozenBy = deepFreezeLoaded(structuredClone(by));\n        }\n        catch {\n            throw new Error(`Invalid generated by for operation ${JSON.stringify(opName)}: ` +\n                'predicates must be serializable data.');\n        }\n        // T04b-preview input array markers (engine-local channel): entries must\n        // name loaded operations/inputs with boolean markers, fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid input array markers for operation ${JSON.stringify(opName)}.`);\n            }\n            for (const [inputName, marker] of Object.entries(opArrays)) {\n                if (!seenInputs.has(inputName)) {\n                    fail('dangling_reference', `Invalid input array marker ${JSON.stringify(inputName)} on operation ` +\n                        `${JSON.stringify(opName)}: no such input.`);\n                }\n                if (!isRecord(marker) || typeof marker['required'] !== 'boolean') {\n                    fail('malformed_descriptor',    descriptor: deepFreezeLoaded(descriptor),\n            by: frozenBy,\n            ...(when !== undefined ? { when: deepFreezeLoaded(when) } : {}),\n            inputArrays:            fail('malformed_descriptor', `Invalid ${what}: input fields need a kind tag.`);\n            }\n            const inputKind = tag['kind'];\n            if 'public')));\n}\n/**\n * T18: resolve one closed-set server initializer (creation only, omitted\n * fields only — `serverOnly` rejects every caller-supplied value, so\n * these fields always arrive omitted). `actor` stamps the row's own\n * attribution identity as a wire `{id}` user value; `now` stamps the\n * frozen invocation clock (retry- and replay-stable: fence retries\n * re-execute pre-commit, while replays return the committed row instead\n * of re-evaluating); `random_secret` mints 256-bit opaque hex material\n * per execution — stable per COMMITTED operation identity through that\n * same replay path (the receipt records it; a retry that re-executes\n * has committed nothing yet). Randomness comes from the ambient\n * `globalThis.crypto` port (node and workerd both provide it — the same\n * seam `replay.ts` hashes with).\n */\nfunction evalServerInit(init, now, actor) {\n    if (init === 'actor') {\n        return { id: actor };\n    }\n    if (init === 'now') {\n        if (!Number.isFinite(now)) {\n            throw new Error('Mutation pipeline needs a finite context.now to resolve server=now.');\n        }\n        return new Date(now).toISOString();\n    }\n    const bytes = new Uint8Array(32);\n    globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues(bytes);\n    let hex = '';\n    for (const byte of bytes) {\n        hex += byte.toString(16).padStart(2, '0');\n    }\n    return hex;\n}\n/** Prototype-safe property definition for caller-keyed candidate objects. */\nfunction safeSet(target, key, value) {\n    Object.defineProperty(target, key, {\n        value,\n        enumerable: true,\n        writable: true,\n        configurable: true,\n    });\n}\n/** Deep-freeze staged rows so invariant views cannot mutate provisional state. */\nfunction deepFreeze(value, seen = new Set()) {\n    if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || seen.has(value)) {\n        return value;\n    }\n    seen.add(value);\n    if (Array.isArray(value)) {\n        for (const entry of value) {\n            deepFreeze(entry, seen);\n        }\n    }\n    else {\n        for (const entry of Object.values(value)) {\n            deepFreeze(entry, seen);\n        }\n    }\n    return Object.freeze(value);\n}\n/**\n * Data-only dot-path read (arrays are opaque leaves, mirroring\n * `resolveRowPath`). Missing or untraversable paths yield `undefined`.\n */\nfunction getDataPath(data, path) {\n    let current = data;\n    for (const segment of path.split('.')) {\n        if (typeof current !== 'object' || current === null || Array.isArray(current)) {\n            return undefined;\n        }\n        const obj = current;\n        if (!Object.hasOwn(obj, segment)) {\n            return undefined;\n        }\n        current = obj[segment];\n    }\n    return current;\n}\n/**\n * Reference equality by target id: interim values are plain `{ id }`, so two\n * values with the same non-empty string id are unchanged (extra keys, if any,\n * are ignored).\n */\nfunction refValuesEqual(oldValue, newValue) {\n    if (Object.is(oldValue, newValue)) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    if (typeof oldValue !== 'object' || oldValue === null || Array.isArray(oldValue)) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    if (typeof newValue !== 'object' || newValue === null || Array.isArray(newValue)) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    const oldId = oldValue['id'];\n    const newId = newValue['id'];\n    return typeof oldId === 'string' && oldId !== '' && oldId === newId;\n}\n/**\n * Evaluate an ordered batch of mutation writes. Per-write order: resolve the\n * model def, load `before` (provisional-aware), build the candidate, run\n * hooks, check `when`/locks/refs, stage uniques, provisionalize, and record\n * history. Invariants run once after ALL writes provisionalize, in write\n * order then def order (a model touched twice runs its invariants twice),\n * each seeing the final provisional state.\n *\n * T31 (Rule A): create/update hooks may stage secondary writes\n * (create/set on other models, same-model barred) plus schedule/cancel\n * timer ops. Staged writes join the work queue immediately after their\n * trigger in staging order and run the identical per-write path minus CRUD\n * hooks (flat, no cascade); hooks evaluate once, in written order, against\n * the proposed state. Staged writes observe the trigger's provisional row\n * (pending parents resolve) plus earlier staged rows, reserve their own\n * versions, enroll in the same fence via the single batch commit, and\n * record history under the triggering operation's identity. Any staged\n * failure voids the whole batch before commit (atomic rollback).\n *\n * B1: same-batch self-canceling writes (create+remove, update+remove one\n * id) net their uniques in the pipeline: a hard remove drops every claim\n * the batch staged for its record and releases the first-touch\n * (committed) keys, so no claim dangles on a removed row and no\n * committed claim strands. (Same-batch double-touch of one row — e.g. a\n * staged update to a staged create — still fails at commit: adapters\n * pre-check every expectedVersion against stored state, so chained\n * provisional versions conflict. Staged writes inherit exactly the\n * caller multi-write rule.)\n */\nexport async function runMutationWrites(input) {\n    const { table, writes, context, store } = input;\n    const now = context.now;\n    const actor = actorFor(context);\n    // T32b-wire: the transitive facility's trigger point. Revision + owner\n    // ONLY — the trigger's enrolled dependencies never enter the pipeline,\n    // so hook bodies cannot inherit them. Without a trigger the owner falls\n    // back to team ?? app, mirroring admission's checkpoint owner.\n    const transitiveTriggerRevision = input.trigger?.revision ?? null;\n    const transitiveOwner = input.trigger?.owner ?? context.team?.teamId ?? context.app;\n    const provisional = new Map();\n    const outWrites = [];\n    const outHistory = [];\n    const outClaims = [];\n    const outReleases = [];\n    const resolvedDefaults = {};\n    const outSchedules = [];\n    const touchedDefs = [];\n    /**\n     * B1: first-touch before-rows per record (committed state at batch\n     * start, or null for batch-created rows). Hard removes release unique\n     * keys from the FIRST touch — not the provisional before — so\n     * multi-touch batches (update+remove, create+remove) free exactly the\n     * committed keys and never claim-then-dangle.\n     */\n    const firstBefore = new Map();\n    /**\n     * B1: resolved-default attribution per batch (field name to the tag\n     * of the write that first resolved it). A second write resolving the\n     * same name rejects LOUD — flat receipts cannot attribute two\n     * resolutions of one name.\n     */\n    const defaultWriters = new Map();\n    /** B1: monotonic per-write tag counter (queue indices shift on splice). */\n    let processedWrites = 0;\n    /** Provisional-aware load: staged rows win, removals mask, else the store. */\n    const getRow = async (model, id) => {\n        const entry = provisional.get(keyOf(model, id));\n        if (entry !== undefined) {\n            return entry.status === 'row' ? entry.row : null;\n        }\n        return store.load(model, id);\n    };\n    /** Full-model scan (archived included) with provisional merged over it. */\n    const scanModel = async (model) => {\n        const base = await store.query({ model, authority: 'owner', archived: 'include' });\n        const merged = new Map();\n        for (const row of base) {\n            merged.set(keyOf(model, row.id), row);\n        }\n        const prefix = `${model}\\0`;\n        for (const [key, entry] of provisional) {\n            if (!key.startsWith(prefix)) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if (entry.status === 'row') {\n                merged.set(key, entry.row);\n            }\n            else {\n                merged.delete(key);\n            }\n        }\n        return [...merged.values()];\n    };\n    /** Required check: missing keys, nulls, and hook-set undefined all fail. */\n    const checkRequired = (candidate, def) => {\n        for (const [field, fieldDef] of Object.entries(def.fields)) {\n            if (!fieldDef.required) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            const value = candidate[field];\n            if (!Object.hasOwn(candidate, field) || value === null || value === undefined) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `Missing required field ${JSON.stringify(field)}.`);\n            }\n        }\n    };\n    /** Create data / update patch normalization (`undefined` reads as `{}`). */\n    const asDataObject = (value, what) => {\n        if (value === undefined) {\n            return {};\n        }\n        if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${what} must be an object.`);\n        }\n        return value;\n    };\n    /** Copy caller data in, rejecting unknown and server-only fields. */\n    const applyCallerData = (target, data, def) => {\n        for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(data)) {\n            const fieldDef = def.fields[field];\n            if (fieldDef === undefined) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `Unknown field ${JSON.stringify(field)} for model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)}.`);\n            }\n            // Patch/data keys with `undefined` values are IGNORED (absent): they\n            // neither set nor delete. `null` is a real value (fails `required`).\n            if (value === undefined) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if (fieldDef.serverOnly) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `Field ${JSON.stringify(field)} is server-only and cannot be supplied.`);\n            }\n            safeSet(target, field, jsonClone(value, `Field ${JSON.stringify(field)}`));\n        }\n    };\n    /**\n     * Post-hook field-name check: hooks may set server-only fields, but never\n     * undeclared ones — downstream readers assume the model contract. Runs on\n     * every path after hooks (caller data was already checked on the way in).\n     */\n    const checkKnownFields = (candidate, def) => {\n        for (const field of Object.keys(candidate)) {\n            if (!Object.hasOwn(def.fields, field)) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `Unknown field ${JSON.stringify(field)} for model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)}.`);\n            }\n        }\n    };\n    /**\n     * Post-hook JSON-safety probe: bigints and circular refs survive cloning\n     * but crash commit-time JSON encoding with a raw TypeError. Reject them as\n     * caller validation instead (bigint money minors stay rejected interim\n     * until the L2 codec join, matching the S4 read stance).\n     */\n    const checkJsonSafe = (candidate, def) => {\n        try {\n            JSON.stringify(candidate);\n        }\n        catch {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `Candidate for model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)} holds non-JSON values.`);\n        }\n    };\n    /**\n     * T31 (Rule A) stage-time validation for one hook-staged write: shape,\n     * create/set-only (staged deletes barred), known model (programmer bug\n     * otherwise, mirroring the pipeline's unknown-model rule), and the\n     * same-model bar — triggering-path recursion, same-model-via-different-op,\n     * and pending-source deletion all name the trigger model, so one bar\n     * covers all three. Returns an engine-owned queue entry. State-dependent\n     * checks (refs, locks, uniques, versions) run later on the shared\n     * per-write path, attributed to the staging hook via the queue entry.\n     */\n    const checkStagedWrite = (def, hookName, staged) => {\n        const hookTag = `Hook ${JSON.stringify(hookName)} on model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)}`;\n        if (typeof staged !== 'object' || staged === null || Array.isArray(staged)) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a write that must be an object.`);\n        }\n        const stagedOp = staged.op;\n        if (stagedOp !== 'create' && stagedOp !== 'update') {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} cannot stage ${JSON.stringify(stagedOp)} writes; hooks stage create/set only.`);\n        }\n        // Validated above: only create/set stage.\n        const op = stagedOp;\n        const stagedModel = staged.model;\n        if (typeof stagedModel !== 'string' || stagedModel === '') {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a write with no model.`);\n        }\n        if (!table.has(stagedModel)) {\n            throw new Error(`${hookTag} staged a write to unknown model ${JSON.stringify(stagedModel)}.`);\n        }\n        if (stagedModel === def.model) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} cannot stage same-model writes; got ${JSON.stringify(op)} on ` +\n                `${JSON.stringify(stagedModel)} (triggering-path recursion and pending-source ` +\n                'deletion are barred).');\n        }\n        const stagedId = staged.id;\n        if (typeof stagedId !== 'string' || stagedId === '') {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a write needing a non-empty string record id.`);\n        }\n        const stagedData = staged.data;\n        if (stagedData !== undefined &&\n            (typeof stagedData !== 'object' || stagedData === null || Array.isArray(stagedData))) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a write whose data must be an object.`);\n        }\n        const stagedParent = staged.parent;\n        let parent;\n        if (stagedParent !== undefined) {\n            if (op !== 'create') {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged an update carrying a parent; parent linkage is immutable.`);\n            }\n            if (typeof stagedParent !== 'object' ||\n                stagedParent === null ||\n                Array.isArray(stagedParent)) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a write with an invalid parent reference.`);\n            }\n            const parentRecord = stagedParent;\n            const parentModel = parentRecord['model'];\n            const parentId = parentRecord['id'];\n            if (typeof parentModel !== 'string' ||\n                parentModel === '' ||\n                typeof parentId !== 'string' ||\n                parentId === '') {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a write with an invalid parent reference.`);\n            }\n            parent = { model: parentModel, id: parentId };\n        }\n        return {\n            hook: hookName,\n            write: {\n                op,\n                model: stagedModel,\n                id: stagedId,\n                ...(parent !== undefined ? { parent } : {}),\n                ...(stagedData !== undefined\n                    ? { data: jsonClone(stagedData, `${hookTag} staged data`) }\n                    : {}),\n            },\n        };\n    };\n    /**\n     * T31 (Rule A) stage-time validation for one hook-staged timer replace:\n     * the S6 schedule shape (bounded non-empty key, finite `at` >= 0,\n     * non-empty event, JSON-safe payload object), attributed to the staging\n     * hook. The invoke boundary re-validates before commit (defense in depth).\n     */\n    const checkStagedSchedule = (def, hookName, replacement) => {\n        const hookTag = `Hook ${JSON.stringify(hookName)} on model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)}`;\n        if (typeof replacement !== 'object' ||\n            replacement === null ||\n            Array.isArray(replacement)) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a schedule that must be an object.`);\n        }\n        const raw = replacement;\n        const key = raw['key'];\n        if (typeof key !== 'string' || key === '') {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a schedule with no key.`);\n        }\n        if (key.length > STAGING_MAX_ID_LENGTH) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a schedule key exceeding ${STAGING_MAX_ID_LENGTH} characters.`);\n        }\n        const at = raw['at'];\n        if (typeof at !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(at) || at < 0) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a schedule with an invalid time; want a finite number >= 0.`);\n        }\n        const event = raw['event'];\n        if (typeof event !== 'string' || event === '') {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a schedule with no event.`);\n        }\n        const payload = raw['payload'];\n        if (typeof payload !== 'object' || payload === null || Array.isArray(payload)) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a schedule whose payload must be an object.`);\n        }\n        const cloned = jsonClone(payload, `${hookTag} staged schedule payload`);\n        checkJsonEncoding(cloned, `${hookTag} staged schedule payload`);\n        return { op: 'replace', key, at, event: event, payload: cloned };\n    };\n    /** T31 (Rule A) stage-time validation for one hook-staged timer cancel. */\n    const checkStagedCancel = (def, hookName, key) => {\n        const hookTag = `Hook ${JSON.stringify(hookName)} on model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)}`;\n        if (typeof key !== 'string' || key === '') {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a cancel with no key.`);\n        }\n        if (key.length > STAGING_MAX_ID_LENGTH) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} staged a cancel key exceeding ${STAGING_MAX_ID_LENGTH} characters.`);\n        }\n        return { op: 'cancel', key };\n    };\n    /**\n     * Run matching hooks in written order; each gets a clone, returns next.\n     * T31 (Rule A): each hook also gets a staging context — `before` is a\n     * deep-frozen snapshot (mutation attempts throw), and `stage`/`schedule`/\n     * `cancel` collect into `sink` (all three reject on remove-op hooks:\n     * delete hooks reject by throwing, never stage). Hook bodies evaluate\n     * once, in written order, against the proposed state.\n     */\n    const runHooks = async (def, op, candidate, before, triggerId, sink) => {\n        let current = candidate;\n        // Frozen once per op and shared across hooks in written order: no hook\n        // can mutate the snapshot a later hook (or the pipeline's own\n        // lock/ref/unique/history reads) observes.\n        const frozenBefore = before === null ? null : deepFreeze(jsonClone(before, 'Hook before'));\n        for (const hook of def.hooks) {\n            if (!hook.ops.includes(op)) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            const hookTag = `Hook ${JSON.stringify(hook.name)} on model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)}`;\n            const forbidStagingOnRemove = (what) => {\n                if (op === 'remove') {\n                    throw new StateError('validation', `${hookTag} runs on a delete and cannot stage ${what}; only create/update hooks stage.`);\n                }\n            };\n            const ctx = {\n                before: frozenBefore,\n                op,\n                actor,\n                now,\n                triggerModel: def.model,\n                triggerId,\n                stage: (staged) => {\n                    forbidStagingOnRemove('secondary writes');\n                    sink.writes.push(checkStagedWrite(def, hook.name, staged));\n                },\n                schedule: (replacement) => {\n                    forbidStagingOnRemove('timers');\n                    sink.schedules.push(checkStagedSchedule(def, hook.name, replacement));\n                },\n                cancel: (key) => {\n                    forbidStagingOnRemove('timers');\n                    sink.schedules.push(checkStagedCancel(def, hook.name, key));\n                },\n                // T32b-wire: hook bodies are transitive effects — fresh scopes at\n                // the CURRENT revision (zero inherited deps) plus re-reads of\n                // CURRENT committed rows at those scopes. `load` deliberately\n                // bypasses the provisional map (`store.load`, never `getRow`):\n                // transitive re-reads observe committed authority state, never\n                // this batch's uncommitted rows.\n                transitive: {\n                    triggerRevision: transitiveTriggerRevision,\n                    owner: transitiveOwner,\n                    openScope: () => openTransitiveScope(store, transitiveOwner),\n                    load: async (scope, model, id) => {\n                        const row = await store.load(model, id);\n                        if (row !== null) {\n                            scope.enroll({ kind: 'record', model, id, version: row.version });\n                        }\n                        return row;\n                    },\n                },\n            };\n            // Each hook gets a clone and its return is re-cloned: hooks can neither\n            // mutate the pipeline candidate nor smuggle uncloneable values forward\n            // (or retain an alias and mutate it after returning).\n            const next = await hook.run(jsonClone(current, 'Hook candidate'), ctx);\n            if (typeof next !== 'object' || next === null || Array.isArray(next)) {\n                throw new Error(`${hookTag} must return a candidate object.`);\n            }\n            current = jsonClone(next, 'Hook result');\n        }\n        return current;\n    };\n    /** Candidate precondition: false reads as `rule_failed`, never silent. */\n    const checkWhen = (when, probe) => {\n        if (when !== undefined && !evalPredicateForRow(when, probe)) {\n            throw new StateError('rule_failed', 'Precondition failed.');\n        }\n    };\n    /** Lock check against the PRE-state row (provisional-before-this-write). */\n    const checkLocks = (def, before) => {\n        for (const lock of def.locks) {\n            if (evalPredicateForRow(lock.when, before)) {\n                throw new StateError('rule_failed', 'Record is locked.');\n            }\n        }\n    };\n    /**\n     * Reference check: on create every present ref is validated; on update only\n     * refs whose value DIFFERS from before (unchanged refs pass untouched, even\n     * when their target has since archived). Values must be `{ id }`, targets\n     * must exist and be unarchived.\n     */\n    const checkRefs = async (def, candidate, before) => {\n        for (const ref of def.refs) {\n            const value = getDataPath(candidate, ref.field);\n            if (value === undefined) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if (before !== null && refValuesEqual(getDataPath(before.data, ref.field), value)) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `Invalid reference in field ${JSON.stringify(ref.field)}.`);\n            }\n            const targetId = value['id'];\n            if (typeof targetId !== 'string' || targetId === '') {\n                throw new StateError('validation', `Invalid reference in field ${JSON.stringify(ref.field)}.`);\n            }\n            const target = await getRow(ref.model, targetId);\n            if (target === null) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', 'Invalid reference.');\n            }\n            if (target.archivedAt !== null) {\n                throw new StateError('validation', 'References to archived records are blocked.');\n            }\n        }\n    };\n    /**\n     * Unique-key canonicalization: strings as-is; numbers/booleans via\n     * `String()`; bigints via `toString()`; null/undefined/missing claim\n     * nothing (nulls are not unique-constrained); anything else is a caller\n     * error, never a silent skip.\n     */\n    const canonicalUnique = (value, key, def) => {\n        if (value === null || value === undefined) {\n            return null;\n        }\n        if (typeof value === 'string') {\n            return value;\n        }\n        if (typeof value === 'number' || typeof value === 'boolean' || typeof value === 'bigint') {\n            return String(value);\n        }\n        throw new StateError('validation', `Unique field ${JSON.stringify(key)} on model ${JSON.stringify(def.model)} ` +\n            'must be a scalar value.');\n    };\n    /**\n     * Disposal scan for hard removes: every ref path of every table model is\n     * scanned (archived included, provisional merged); any live value pointing\n     * at the target rejects. A referrer removed EARLIER in the batch already\n     * masks itself; one removed later still blocks — order co-removals\n     * referrer-first.\n     */\n    const checkDisposal = async (targetModel, targetId) => {\n        for (const [model, modelDef] of table) {\n            if (modelDef.refs.length === 0) {\n                continue;\n            }\n            const rows = await scanModel(model);\n            for (const row of rows) {\n                for (const ref of modelDef.refs) {\n                    if (ref.model !== targetModel) {\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    const value = getDataPath(row.data, ref.field);\n                    if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) {\n                        continue;\n                    }\n                    if (value['id'] === targetId) {\n                        throw new StateError('rule_failed', 'Cannot remove: incoming references exist.');\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    };\n    /** Record one history entry with full before/after data (authority record). */\n    const recordHistory = (entry) => {\n        outHistory.push({\n            model: entry.model,\n            recordId: entry.recordId,\n            version: entry.version,\n            operation: context.operation,\n            operationId: context.operationId,\n            actor,\n            at: now,\n            change: entry.change,\n            before: entry.before === null ? null : structuredClone(entry.before.data),\n            after: entry.after === null ? null : structuredClone(entry.after),\n        });\n    };\n    /**\n     * B1: record one resolved default under the flat batch receipt map,\n     * rejecting LOUD when another write already resolved the same name.\n     * `tag` identifies the resolving write (op + model + id + sequence).\n     * Same-write double recording is impossible (the create path visits\n     * each field once), so any second tag is a genuine cross-write\n     * collision — last-wins would persist silently without this throw.\n     */\n    const recordDefault = (field, value, tag) => {\n        const first = defaultWriters.get(field);\n        if (first !== undefined && first !== tag) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', `Resolved-default collision in one mutation batch: field ${JSON.stringify(field)} ` +\n                `defaulted by both ${first} and ${tag}; receipts record resolved defaults once ` +\n                'per batch, so split the batch or rename the field.');\n        }\n        defaultWriters.set(field, tag);\n        safeSet(resolvedDefaults, field, value);\n    };\n    /**\n     * B1: scenario-parity archived-target gate. Code and message are EXACTLY\n     * admission's (`validation` / `Archived records cannot be used here.`):\n     * the CRUD executors inherit this verdict from admission, and gated\n     * pipeline callers (the scenario seam) must agree with it verdict for\n     * verdict. Runs before hooks — admission gates before execution too.\n     */\n    const checkGatedArchivedTarget = (before, gateOn) => {\n        if (gateOn && before.archivedAt !== null) {\n            throw new StateError('validation', 'Archived records cannot be used here.');\n        }\n    };\n    // T31 (Rule A): the work queue starts as the caller writes; each\n    // trigger write's staged secondaries splice in immediately after it, in\n    // staging order, so staged writes observe the trigger's provisional row\n    // (pending parents resolve) plus earlier staged rows. Staged entries skip\n    // hooks (flat, no cascade) and stage nothing further.\n    const queue = writes.map((write) => ({ write, stagedBy: null }));\n    for (let index = 0; index < queue.length; index += 1) {\n        const entry = queue[index];\n        if (entry === undefined) {\n            throw new Error('Mutation queue misaligned.');\n        }\n        const write = entry.write;\n        // Null for caller writes (hooks run into `sink`); the staging hook's\n        // name for staged writes (hooks skipped, sink stays empty).\n        const stagedBy = entry.stagedBy;\n        const sink = { writes: [], schedules: [] };\n        /** Drain this write's staged secondaries into the queue + schedules. */\n        const drainSink = () => {\n            if (sink.writes.length === 0 && sink.schedules.length === 0) {\n                return;\n            }\n            queue.splice(index + 1, 0, ...sink.writes.map((staged) => ({ write: staged.write, stagedBy: staged.hook })));\n            outSchedules.push(...sink.schedules);\n        };\n        const def = table.get(write.model);\n        if (def === undefined) {\n            // Unknown models are programmer bugs: models come from program defs,\n            // never from caller input.\n            throw new Error(`Unknown model in mutation write: ${JSON.stringify(write.model)}.`);\n        }\n        touchedDefs.push(def);\n        const id = write.id;\n        if (typeof id !== 'string' || id === '') {\n            throw new StateError('validation', 'Mutation writes need a non-empty string record id.');\n        }\n        // Admission pre-loads update/remove targets, but the pipeline re-loads\n        // via the provisional map for uniformity (batch-earlier writes visible).\n        const before = await getRow(write.model, id);\n        // B1: first-touch before-row (committed state at batch start; null for\n        // batch-created rows). Stale or missing rows fail with kind 'version'.\n */\nasync function checkWriteVersions(db, batch) {\n    for (const write of batch.writes) {\n        if (write.kind !== 'update' && write.kind !== 'remove') {\n            continue;\n        }\n        const row = await db\n            .prepare('SELECT version, updated, updated_by FROM records WHERE model = ? AND id = ?')\n            .bind(write.model, write.id)\n            .first();\n        const expected = write.expectedVersion;\n        const where = `${write.model}/${write.id}`;\n        if (row === null) {\n            throw new StorageConstraintError('version', `version mismatch for ${where}: expected ${expected}, row is missing`);\n        }\n        if (row.version !== expected) {\n            throw new StorageConstraintError('version', `version mismatch for ${where}: expected ${expected}, stored ${row.version}`, {\n                model: write.model,\n                id: write.id,\n                version: row.version,\n                updated: row.updated,\n                updatedBy: row.updated_by,\n            });\n        }\n    }\n}\nasync function readRevisionInner(db) {\n    const row = await db\n        .prepare('SELECT revision FROM fence WHERE id = ?')\n        .bind(FENCE_ROW_ID)\n        .first();\n    if (row === null) {\n        throw new Error('schema not initialized: fence row is missing (run ensureSchema first)');\n    }\n    return row.revision;\n}\n/** Map a failed-batch error to the storage error classes. Never throws. */\nasync function toCommitError(db, expected, error) {\n    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    if (message.includes('fence_log')) {\n        let actual = null;\n        try {\n            actual = await readRevisionInner(db);\n        }\n        catch {\n            actual = null;\n        }\n        return new FenceConflictError(expected, actual);\n    }\n    if (message.includes('unique_claims') || message.includes('outbox')) {\n        return new StorageConstraintError('unique', message);\n    }\n    if (message.includes('receipts')) {\n        return new StorageConstraintError('receipt_reuse', message);\n    }\n    return new StorageConstraintError('unknown', message);\n}\nconst RECEIPT_COLUMNS = 'app, owner, principal, operation, operation_id, input_hash, ' +\n    'resolved_defaults, outcome, committed_revision, created_at';\nfunction toReceipt(row) {\n    return {\n        identity: {\n            app: row.app,\n            owner: row.owner,\n            principal: row.principal,\n            operation: row.operation,\n            operationId: row.operation_id,\n        },\n        inputHash: row.input_hash,\n        resolvedDefaults: JSON.parse(row.resolved_defaults),\n        outcome: JSON.parse(row.outcome),\n        committedRevision: row.committed_revision,\n        createdAt: row.created_at,\n    };\n}\nconst OUTBOX_COLUMNS = 'intent_id, operation, operation_id, target, arguments, occurrence_index, dispatch_guard, ' +\n    'handler_contract';\nfunction toOutboxIntent(row) {\n    return {\n        intentId: row.intent_id,\n        operation: row.operation,\n        operationId: row.operation_id,\n        target: row.target,\n        arguments: JSON.parse(row.arguments),\n        occurrenceIndex: row.occurrence_index,\n        // NULL guard stays absent (never explicit undefined: exactOptionalPropertyTypes).\n        ...(row.dispatch_guard === null ? {} : { dispatchGuard: row.dispatch_guard }),\n        // B3: NULL contract stays absent (pre-B3 rows attest at the boundary).\n        ...(row.handler_contract === null ? {} : { handlerContract: row.handler_contract }),\n    };\n}\nconst SCHEDULE_COLUMNS = '\"key\", at, event, payload';\nfunction toScheduleEntry(row) {\n    return {\n        key: row.key,\n        at: row.at,\n        event: row.event,\n        payload: JSON.parse(row.payload),\n    };\n}\nconst HISTORY_COLUMNS = 'model, record_id, version, operation, operation_id, actor, at, change, \"before\", \"after\"';\nfunction toHistoryEntry(row) {\n    return {\n        model: row.model,\n        recordId: row.record_id,\n        version: row.version,\n        operation: row.operation,\n        operationId: row.operation_id,\n        actor: row.actor,\n        at: row.at,\n        change: row.change,\n        before: row.before === null ? null : JSON.parse(row.before),\n        after: row.after === null ? null : JSON.parse(row.after),\n    };\n}\nconst SNAPSHOT_COLUMNS = 'owner, snapshot_id, digest, installed_revision, installed_at';\nfunction toInstalledSnapshot(row) {\n    return {\n        owner: row.owner,\n        snapshotId: row.snapshot_id,\n        digest: row.digest,\n        installedRevision: row.installed_revision,\n        installedAt: row.installed_at,\n    };\n}\nconst STAGING_COLUMNS = 'target_model, record_id, version, data, parent, converted, created, created_by, archived_at';\nfunction toStagedRow(row) {\n    return {\n        targetModel: row.target_model,\n        recordId: row.record_id,\n        version: row.version,\n        data: JSON.parse(row.data),\n        parent: row.parent === null ? null : JSON.parse(row.parent),\n        converted: row.converted === 1,\n        // NULL stays absent (never explicit undefined: exactOptionalPropertyTypes).\n        ...(row.created === null ? {} : { created: row.created }),\n        ...(row.created_by === null ? {} : { createdBy: row.created_by }),\n        ...(row.archived_at === null ? {} : { archivedAt: row.archived_at }),\n    };\n}\nconst PROGRESS_COLUMNS = 'migration_id, phase, staged_cursor, publish_cursor, updated_revision';\nfunction toMigrationProgress(row) {\n    return {\n        migrationId: row.migration_id,\n        phase: row.phase,\n        stagedCursor: row.staged_cursor === null ? null : JSON.parse(row.staged_cursor),\n        publishCursor: row.publish_cursor === null ? null : JSON.parse(row.publish_cursor),\n        updatedRevision: row.updated_revision,\n    };\n}\nconst OUTCOME_COLUMNS = 'migration_id, kind, intent_id, handler_contract';\nfunction toMigrationOutcome(row) {\n    return {\n        migrationId: row.migration_id,\n        kind: row.kind,\n        intentId: row.intent_id,\n        handlerContract: row.handler_contract,\n    };\n}\nconst FAILURE_COLUMNS = 'migration_id, leg, prior_phase, staged_cursor, publish_cursor, error, at, revision';\nfunction toMigrationFailure(row) {\n    return {\n        migrationId: row.migration_id,\n        leg: row.leg,\n        priorPhase: row.prior_phase,\n        stagedCursor: row.staged_cursor === null ? null : JSON.parse(row.staged_cursor),\n        publishCursor: row.publish_cursor === null ? null : JSON.parse(row.publish_cursor),\n        error: row.error,\n        at: row.at,\n        revision: row.revision,\n    };\n}\n/**\n * S7: merge one staged row onto its live target, mirroring the memory\n * adapter exactly. Version/data/parent come from the staged row; creation\n * metadata carries over from the existing live row when present; the\n * matching history entry (same model + record id, first in chunk order)\n * supplies updated/updatedBy — and created/createdBy for rows with no live\n * predecessor. Fallback is 0/''; archivedAt carries over (never unarchives).\n */\nfunction mergePublishedColumns(staged, existing, history) {\n    const match = history.find((entry) => entry.model === staged.targetModel &&\n        entry.recordId === staged.recordId);\n    return {\n        created: staged.created ?? existing?.created ?? match?.at ?? 0,\n        updated: match?.at ?? existing?.updated ?? 0,\n        createdBy: staged.createdBy ?? existing?.created_by ?? match?.actor ?? '',\n        updatedBy: match?.actor ?? existing?.updated_by ?? '',\n        archivedAt: staged.archivedAt ?? existing?.archived_at ?? null,\n    };\n}\n/** D1-backed `StoragePort`. Call `ensureSchema(db)` once before first use. */\nexport function createD1Storage(db) {\n    return {\n        async readRevision() {\n            return readRevisionInner(db);\n        },\n        async load(model, id) {\n            const row = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${RECORD_COLUMNS} FROM records WHERE model = ? AND id = ?`)\n                .bind(model, id)\n                .first();\n            return row === null ? null : toStoredRow(row);\n        },\n        async query(spec) {\n            const bindings = [spec.model];\n            let sql = `SELECT ${RECORD_COLUMNS} FROM records WHERE model = ?`;\n            if (spec.parent !== undefined) {\n                // S5: parent_* columns carry the linkage StoredRow.parent persists, so\n                // this filter scopes positively; NULL-parent rows never match it.\n                sql += ' AND parent_model = ? AND parent_id = ?';\n                bindings.push(spec.parent.model, spec.parent.id);\n            }\n            // S2 excludes archived rows only; content expiry is a later slice.\n            if (spec.archived !== 'include') {\n                sql += ' AND archived_at IS NULL';\n            }\n            if (spec.where !== undefined) {\n                sql += ` AND ${compilePredicate(spec.where, bindings)}`;\n            }\n            sql += ` ORDER BY ${compileOrder(spec.order)}`;\n            if (spec.limit !== undefined) {\n                checkLimit(spec.limit);\n                sql += ' LIMIT ?';\n                bindings.push(spec.limit);\n            }\n            const result = await db.prepare(sql).bind(...bindings).all();\n            return result.results.map(toStoredRow);\n        },\n        async commit(batch) {\n            const expected = batch.expectedRevision;\n            if (!Number.isInteger(expected) || expected < 0) {\n                throw new Error(`Invalid expectedRevision: ${JSON.stringify(batch.expectedRevision)}`);\n            }\n            // The fence INSERT below only proves `expected + 1` is fresh; it cannot\n            // see a *future* expected revision skipping ahead and breaking the\n            // density the scheme rests on. Reject those up front. Race-safe with\n            // zero honest false-positives: revisions are monotonic, so an honest\n            // `expected` (current at read time) can never exceed current later.\n            const current = await readRevisionInner(db);\n            if (expected > current) {\n                throw new FenceConflictError(batch.expectedRevision, current);\n            }\n            await checkWriteVersions(db, batch);\n            const next = expected + 1;\n            // fence_log/outbox timestamps come from the receipt when the batch\n            // carries one; receipt-less batches (tests, bookkeeping) use now.\n            const at = batch.receipt?.createdAt ?? Date.now();\n            const operation = batch.receipt === null\n                ? 'unknown'\n                : batch.receipt.identity.operation;\n            const statements = [\n                db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO fence_log(revision, at, operation) VALUES (?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(next, at, operation),\n                db.prepare('UPDATE fence SET revision = ? WHERE id = ?').bind(next, FENCE_ROW_ID),\n            ];\n            for (const write of batch.writes) {\n                if (write.kind === 'insert') {\n                    statements.push(db\n                        .prepare('INSERT INTO records(model, id, version, created, updated, created_by, ' +\n                        'updated_by, archived_at, owner, parent_model, parent_id, data) ' +\n                        'VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                        .bind(write.model, write.row.id, write.row.version, write.row.created, write.row.updated, write.row.createdBy, write.row.updatedBy, write.row.archivedAt, '', \n                    // S5: persist row.parent (undefined counts as NULL, like null).\n                    write.row.parent?.model ?? null, write.row.parent?.id ?? null, JSON.stringify(write.row.data)));\n                }\n                else if (write.kind === 'update') {\n                    // Unconditional on version inside the batch: expectedVersion was\n                    // pre-validated above, and the fence INSERT serializes writers, so\n                    // a concurrent change aborts the whole batch first.\n                    statements.push(db\n                        .prepare('UPDATE records SET version = ?, updated = ?, updated_by = ?, ' +\n                        'archived_at = ?, parent_model = ?, parent_id = ?, data = ? ' +\n                        'WHERE model = ? AND id = ?')\n                        .bind(write.row.version, write.row.updated, write.row.updatedBy, write.row.archivedAt, \n                    // S5: persist whatever parent the row carries (the engine keeps\n                    // it immutable by carrying before.parent; see contracts).\n                    write.row.parent?.model ?? null, write.row.parent?.id ?? null, JSON.stringify(write.row.data), write.model, write.id));\n                }\n                else {\n                    statements.push(db\n                        .prepare('DELETE FROM records WHERE model = ? AND id = ?')\n                        .bind(write.model, write.id));\n                }\n            }\n            // Releases run before claims so a key can move between records (or be\n            // re-claimed) within one batch without a transient PK collision.\n            for (const release of batch.uniqueReleases) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('DELETE FROM unique_claims WHERE model = ? AND key_name = ? AND key_value = ?')\n                    .bind(release.model, release.keyName, release.keyValue));\n            }\n            for (const claim of batch.uniqueClaims) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO unique_claims(model, key_name, key_value, record_id) ' +\n                    'VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(claim.model, claim.keyName, claim.keyValue, claim.recordId));\n            }\n            for (const entry of batch.history) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO history(model, record_id, version, operation, operation_id, ' +\n                    'actor, at, change, \"before\", \"after\") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(entry.model, entry.recordId, entry.version, entry.operation, entry.operationId, entry.actor, entry.at, entry.change, entry.before === null ? null : JSON.stringify(entry.before), entry.after === null ? null : JSON.stringify(entry.after)));\n            }\n            if (batch.receipt !== null) {\n                const receipt = batch.receipt;\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO receipts(app, owner, principal, operation, operation_id, ' +\n                    'input_hash, resolved_defaults, outcome, committed_revision, created_at) ' +\n                    'VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(receipt.identity.app, receipt.identity.owner, receipt.identity.principal, receipt.identity.operation, receipt.identity.operationId, receipt.inputHash, JSON.stringify(receipt.resolvedDefaults), JSON.stringify(receipt.outcome), receipt.committedRevision, receipt.createdAt));\n            }\n            for (const intent of batch.outbox) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO outbox(intent_id, operation, operation_id, target, arguments, ' +\n                    'occurrence_index, dispatch_guard, handler_contract, status, created_at) ' +\n                    \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'pending', ?)\")\n                    .bind(intent.intentId, intent.operation, intent.operationId, intent.target, JSON.stringify(intent.arguments), intent.occurrenceIndex, intent.dispatchGuard ?? null, intent.handlerContract ?? null, at));\n            }\n            // S6: acks run AFTER the intent inserts in this same atomic batch, so\n            // acking an id staged in this SAME batch marks it dispatched. One UPDATE\n            // per id; unknown or already-dispatched ids match zero rows (idempotent\n            // no-op — dispatchers retry at-least-once). `undefined` counts as `[]`.\n            for (const intentId of batch.outboxAck ?? []) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare(\"UPDATE outbox SET status = 'dispatched' WHERE intent_id = ?\")\n                    .bind(intentId));\n            }\n            for (const schedule of batch.schedules) {\n                if (schedule.op === 'replace') {\n                    statements.push(db\n                        .prepare('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO schedules(\"key\", at, event, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                        .bind(schedule.key, schedule.at, schedule.event, JSON.stringify(schedule.payload)));\n                }\n                else {\n                    statements.push(db.prepare('DELETE FROM schedules WHERE \"key\" = ?').bind(schedule.key));\n                }\n            }\n            try {\n                await db.batch(statements);\n            }\n            catch (error) {\n                throw await toCommitError(db, batch.expectedRevision, error);\n            }\n            return { revision: next };\n        },\n        async readReceipt(identity) {\n            const row = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${RECEIPT_COLUMNS} FROM receipts WHERE app = ? AND owner = ? AND ` +\n                'principal = ? AND operation = ? AND operation_id = ?')\n                .bind(identity.app, identity.owner, identity.principal, identity.operation, identity.operationId)\n                .first();\n            return row === null ? null : toReceipt(row);\n        },\n        async outboxPending() {\n            // S6: pending only, deterministic (created_at, intent_id) order —\n            // identical ordering to the memory adapter's comparator.\n            const result = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${OUTBOX_COLUMNS} FROM outbox WHERE status = 'pending' ` +\n                'ORDER BY created_at, intent_id')\n                .all();\n            return result.results.map(toOutboxIntent);\n        },\n        async scheduleGet(key) {\n            const row = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${SCHEDULE_COLUMNS} FROM schedules WHERE \"key\" = ?`)\n                .bind(key)\n                .first();\n            return row === null ? null : toScheduleEntry(row);\n        },\n        async schedulesDue(now, limit) {\n            checkSchedulesLimit(limit);\n            const result = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${SCHEDULE_COLUMNS} FROM schedules WHERE at <= ? ORDER BY at, \"key\" LIMIT ?`)\n                .bind(now, limit)\n                .all();\n            return result.results.map(toScheduleEntry);\n        },\n        async historyFor(model, recordId) {\n            const result = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${HISTORY_COLUMNS} FROM history WHERE model = ? AND record_id = ? ` +\n                // S6 review: `seq` tiebreaks duplicate versions (reachable only via\n                // direct unstaged commits); fenced writes carry unique versions.\n                'ORDER BY version, seq')\n                .bind(model, recordId)\n                .all();\n            return result.results.map(toHistoryEntry);\n        },\n        async readInstalledSnapshot(owner) {\n            // S7: null when the owner was never installed (fresh installs take a\n            // separate path and never apply transitions).\n            const row = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${SNAPSHOT_COLUMNS} FROM snapshots WHERE owner = ?`)\n                .bind(owner)\n                .first();\n            return row === null ? null : toInstalledSnapshot(row);\n        },\n        async readMigrationProgress(migrationId) {\n            // S7: null when the migration never staged anything.\n            const row = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${PROGRESS_COLUMNS} FROM migration_progress WHERE migration_id = ?`)\n                .bind(migrationId)\n                .first();\n            return row === null ? null : toMigrationProgress(row);\n        },\n        async readStagedRows(migrationId, cursor, limit) {\n            // S7: (model, record id) order after the cursor, capped at limit.\n            checkStagedRowsLimit(limit);\n            const bindings = [migrationId];\n            let sql = `SELECT ${STAGING_COLUMNS} FROM migration_staging WHERE migration_id = ?`;\n            if (cursor !== null) {\n                sql += ' AND (target_model > ? OR (target_model = ? AND record_id > ?))';\n                bindings.push(cursor.model, cursor.model, cursor.recordId);\n            }\n            sql += ' ORDER BY target_model, record_id LIMIT ?';\n            bindings.push(limit);\n            const result = await db.prepare(sql).bind(...bindings).all();\n            return result.results.map(toStagedRow);\n        },\n        async stageMigrationRows(input) {\n            // S7: ONE fenced batch: upsert staged rows (idempotent restage by\n            // migration/model/id key) plus the progress row, atomically. The fence\n            // INSERT is the same serialization point as commit's.\n            await checkMigrationExpected(db, input.expectedRevision);\n            const next = input.expectedRevision + 1;\n            const at = Date.now();\n            const statements = [\n                db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO fence_log(revision, at, operation) VALUES (?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(next, at, `migration:stage:${input.migrationId}`),\n                db.prepare('UPDATE fence SET revision = ? WHERE id = ?').bind(next, FENCE_ROW_ID),\n            ];\n            for (const row of input.rows) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO migration_staging(migration_id, target_model, ' +\n                    'record_id, version, data, parent, converted, created, created_by, ' +\n                    'archived_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(input.migrationId, row.targetModel, row.recordId, row.version, JSON.stringify(row.data), row.parent === null ? null : JSON.stringify(row.parent), row.converted ? 1 : 0, row.created ?? null, row.createdBy ?? null, row.archivedAt ?? null));\n            }\n            statements.push(db\n                .prepare('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO migration_progress(migration_id, phase, staged_cursor, ' +\n                'publish_cursor, updated_revision) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                .bind(input.migrationId, input.progress.phase, input.progress.stagedCursor === null\n                ? null\n                : JSON.stringify(input.progress.stagedCursor), input.progress.publishCursor === null\n                ? null\n                : JSON.stringify(input.progress.publishCursor), input.progress.updatedRevision));\n            try {\n                await db.batch(statements);\n            }\n            catch (error) {\n                throw await toCommitError(db, input.expectedRevision, error);\n            }\n            return { revision: next };\n        },\n        async publishMigrationChunk(input) {\n            // S7: ONE fenced batch: upsert live records from staged rows at their\n            // target versions, insert history, dispose drops (remove + drop\n            // history), and upsert progress — atomically. Existing live rows are\n            // pre-read for metadata carry-over (same fence-serialized safety as\n            // checkWriteVersions: a concurrent commit aborts our fence INSERT).\n            await checkMigrationExpected(db, input.expectedRevision);\n            const next = input.expectedRevision + 1;\n            const at = Date.now();\n            const existing = new Map();\n            for (const row of input.rows) {\n                const found = await db\n                    .prepare(`SELECT ${RECORD_COLUMNS} FROM records WHERE model = ? AND id = ?`)\n                    .bind(row.targetModel, row.recordId)\n                    .first();\n                existing.set(`${row.targetModel}\\0${row.recordId}`, found);\n            }\n            const statements = [\n                db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO fence_log(revision, at, operation) VALUES (?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(next, at, `migration:publish:${input.migrationId}`),\n                db.prepare('UPDATE fence SET revision = ? WHERE id = ?').bind(next, FENCE_ROW_ID),\n            ];\n            for (const row of input.rows) {\n                const key = `${row.targetModel}\\0${row.recordId}`;\n                const merged = mergePublishedColumns(row, existing.get(key) ?? null, input.history);\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO records(model, id, version, created, updated, created_by, ' +\n                    'updated_by, archived_at, owner, parent_model, parent_id, data) ' +\n                    'VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(row.targetModel, row.recordId, row.version, merged.created, merged.updated, merged.createdBy, merged.updatedBy, merged.archivedAt, '', row.parent?.model ?? null, row.parent?.id ?? null, JSON.stringify(row.data)));\n            }\n            for (const entry of input.history) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO history(model, record_id, version, operation, operation_id, ' +\n                    'actor, at, change, \"before\", \"after\") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(entry.model, entry.recordId, entry.version, entry.operation, entry.operationId, entry.actor, entry.at, entry.change, entry.before === null ? null : JSON.stringify(entry.before), entry.after === null ? null : JSON.stringify(entry.after)));\n            }\n            for (const drop of input.drops) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('DELETE FROM records WHERE model = ? AND id = ?')\n                    .bind(drop.model, drop.recordId));\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO history(model, record_id, version, operation, operation_id, ' +\n                    'actor, at, change, \"before\", \"after\") VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(drop.history.model, drop.history.recordId, drop.history.version, drop.history.operation, drop.history.operationId, drop.history.actor, drop.history.at, drop.history.change, drop.history.before === null ? null : JSON.stringify(drop.history.before), drop.history.after === null ? null : JSON.stringify(drop.history.after)));\n            }\n            // Claim moves ride the same batch: releases before claims, mirroring\n            // commit, so a model rename moves keys between models atomically.\n            for (const release of input.uniqueReleases ?? []) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('DELETE FROM unique_claims WHERE model = ? AND key_name = ? AND key_value = ?')\n                    .bind(release.model, release.keyName, release.keyValue));\n            }\n            for (const claim of input.uniqueClaims ?? []) {\n                statements.push(db\n                    .prepare('INSERT INTO unique_claims(model, key_name, key_value, record_id) ' +\n                    'VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                    .bind(claim.model, claim.keyName, claim.keyValue, claim.recordId));\n            }\n            statements.push(db\n                .prepare('INSERT OR REPLACE INTO migration_progress(migration_id, phase, staged_cursor, ' +\n                'publish_cursor, updated_revision) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')\n                .bind(input.migrationId, input.progress.phase, input.progress.stagedCursor === null\n                ? null\n                : JSON.stringify(input.progress.stagedCursor), input.progress.publishCursor === null\n                ? null\n                : JSON.stringify(input.progress.publishCursor), input.progress.updatedRevision));\n            try {\n                await db.batch(statements);\n            }\n            catch (error) {\n                throw await toCommitError(db, input.expectedRevision, error);\n            }\n            return { revision: next };\n        },\n        async flipInstalledSnapshot(input) {\n            // S7: idempotent activation. A null snapshot is an owner REMOVAL flip\n            // (dropOwner): the pointer is deleted instead of installed; a removal\n            // against an already-absent pointer is a no-op success. Otherwise ONE\n            // fenced batch: install the pointer, remove the renamed-away owner\n            // pointer, mark invalidated intents skipped, record outcomes, and mark\n            // progress active — atomically.\n            if (input.snapshot === null && input.renameFromOwner !== null) {\n                throw new Error('flipInstalledSnapshot: a removal flip renames nothing.');\n            }\n            if (input.snapshot !== null && input.snapshot.owner !== input.owner) {\n                throw new Error('flipInstalledSnapshot: snapshot.owner must equal the flip owner.');\n            }\n            const installed = await db\n                .prepare(`SELECT ${SNAPSHOT_COLUMNS} FROM snapshots WHERE owner = ?`)\n                .bind(input.owner)\n                .first();\n            if (input.snapshot === null) {\n                if (installed === null) {\n                    return { revision: await readRevisionInner(db), flipped: false };\n                }\n            }\n            else if (installed !== null &&\n                installed.snapshot_id === input.snapshot.snapshotId &&\n                installed.digest === input.snapshot.digest) {\n                return { revision: await readRevisionInner(db), flipped: false };\n            }\n            await checkMigrationExpected(db, input.expectedRevision);\n            const next = input.expectedRevision + 1;\n            const at = Date.now();\n            const snapshotStatement = input.snapshot === null\n                ?
